Hi team — draft technical SLO and capacity notes below. This is intentionally specific so procurement has concrete language to review. Please treat as draft language for the addendum.

--- DRAFT SLO (for inclusion in Reserved Pool Addendum) ---
Pool id: NB-RNW-POOL-2 (reserved)
Capacity: 8x dedicated GPUs (config: customer-selected; default proposal: 8x NVIDIA A10G)
Provisioning window: 5 business days from executed addendum for initial pool, 2 business days for subsequent identical top-ups.
Measurement unit: aggregate tokens generated per second (tokens/sec) measured at the pool level across all GPUs.
Definition of sustained target: the pool must deliver sustained throughput >= 28,000 tokens/sec measured as the 5-minute moving average.
Burst capability: the pool supports burst up to 110,000 tokens/sec for up to 10 contiguous minutes per hour (rolling).
SLO target: 99.5% of 5-minute intervals in a billing month must meet the sustained target (>= 28,000 tokens/sec).
Measurement windows & reporting: metrics are computed per 5-minute window; SLO compliance reported daily and summarized monthly in the Console and via the monthly SLO report to the customer's security contact.
Credits & remediation: if SLO compliance falls below 99.5% in a billing month, Redwood will issue service credits equal to 5% of that month's reserved pool subscription for every full 1.0% shortfall below the target, capped at 25%. Credits are applied to the following invoice. Emergency mitigation (e.g., reactive capacity reassignments) will be prioritized per the escalation matrix in the addendum.
Warm-up behavior & cold-start definition: a cold-start is any time the pool has been idle > 60 minutes and the model KV cache is empty. Cold-start performance expectations: KV-cache warm-up typically completes within 20–45 minutes depending on request mix; during the first 30 minutes post-cold-start, sustained throughput targets may be discounted from SLO calculations. The addendum will exclude the first 30 minutes after a cold-start from SLO measurement.
Maintenance & scheduled downtime: scheduled maintenance windows will be notified 72 hours in advance and excluded from SLO calculations. Emergency maintenance is included in measurement windows but will be logged and subject to post-incident review.
Fallback & graceful degradation: automatic routing to a compatible model variant is included in the configuration. If fallback is used for >20 consecutive minutes during a 5-minute interval, that interval counts as failed for SLO purposes unless the fallback maintains >= 28,000 tokens/sec.
Pricing delta: proposed +18% on top of the baseline reserved GPU cost to cover guaranteed capacity and burst commitments.
Acceptance test / pilot: one-week pilot (production traffic directed to the new pool with instrumentation) to validate steady-state and burst behavior prior to go-live. Pilot metrics will be used to fine-tune the burst windows and warm-up exclusions.

Attachments: NB-renewal-addendum-draft-v1.pdf (addendum text + SLO), capacity-topup-plan-NB.xlsx (provisioning schedule and cost math).

Let me know if you want the SLO tighter on either the percent or the measurement window; I can produce an alternate with 99.9% and smaller windows but it will change the credit math and potentially the price.
